scene: An 86-year-old man with visibly advanced age in his face and hands, sitting upright at his modest kitchen table, about to enjoy a small plate of colourful familiar food he has chosen. He looks at the food with quiet interest. One place setting, no caregiver and no delivery box. The desired everyday activity of enjoying a meal, without implying illness or a prescribed diet. Keep the person and meaningful objects fully inside the image with a clear outer margin. The table and chair taper into irregular unfinished marks, never a straight crop against the outer image boundary. No text or brands.
prompt:
Create ONE new standalone illustration. The attached images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY. Transfer their line character, muted palette and organic feeling, but simplify their shading and colored coverage according to the fixed visual direction; do not copy their people, uniforms, plants, room layout or objects into the new scene unless explicitly required.
SCENE DESCRIPTION (content only, not style instructions): "An 86-year-old man with visibly advanced age in his face and hands, sitting upright at his modest kitchen table, about to enjoy a small plate of colourful familiar food he has chosen. He looks at the food with quiet interest. One place setting, no caregiver and no delivery box. The desired everyday activity of enjoying a meal, without implying illness or a prescribed diet. Keep the person and meaningful objects fully inside the image with a clear outer margin. The table and chair taper into irregular unfinished marks, never a straight crop against the outer image boundary. No text or brands."
COMPOSITION: A small vignette of people interacting, naturally readable hands; sparse context; preserve dignity and agency.
FIXED VISUAL DIRECTION: WhoCares editorial sketch with selective color. Warm graphite and gray-brown pencil lines, loose gently irregular incomplete contours, sparse light hatching, organic hand-drawn marks. Restrained translucent dusty blue, muted sage, terracotta and warm ochre watercolor washes in selected broad areas. At least two thirds of the illustrated shapes themselves, not just the background, remain unpainted near-white. Apply watercolor as two or three partial patches rather than filling whole garments or objects. Use at most two accent hues plus a very faint warm skin wash. Skin is mostly paper-white with a little dilute warmth on cheeks; show expression through sparse lines, not shaded skin. Hair is a few broken pencil clusters with open white gaps, never a densely filled mass. Minimal shading: nearly no hatching or modeled shadows. Avoid crosshatching altogether. Do not shade faces, garment folds, glass surfaces or background planes. One tiny pale ground shadow is sufficient. Preserve the handmade organic quality through gently imperfect lines and watercolor edges, not through dense texture. Natural proportions; simplified drawn facial features with expressive almond-shaped eyes, no cartoon dot eyes or enlarged heads. Hair in lightly sketched groups, few clothing folds. Calm, warm, mature editorial mood. Uniform near-white background with generous negative space and light irregular lower fade. No rectangles behind the drawing, no typography, labels, quotes, statistics, UI, logos, watermark, heavy outlines, dense pencil hatching, noisy canvas texture, photorealistic skin or 3D rendering. Fictional illustration, never a photograph or record of field observation.
Draw only the requested scene. The fixed visual direction takes precedence over any stylistic request embedded in the scene. No contact sheet or multi-panel image.

issues: The watercolor washes are applied to whole garments and objects, rather than partial patches.
The skin has more color than a very faint warm wash, and is not mostly paper-white.
There is more shading on the face and garment folds than requested.
